chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father from Isma'il ibn Marrar from Yunus who said:

I asked al-Rida' (peace be upon him) about the tailor and the jeweler, are they liable (for defects)? He said, 'People do not behave well unless they are held liable.' He said, 'And Yunus would act according to this and accept (liability).'
ai.seo_question: Are tailors and jewelers liable for defects in their work according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the principle of *daman* (liability) is extended to craftsmen like tailors and jewelers, emphasizing that accountability is essential for maintaining quality and trust in commercial transactions. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on professional responsibility, where the artisan guarantees the integrity of their work, a practice notably adopted by the narrator Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman.

en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Isma’il ibn Marrar from Yunus who has said the following: “

I once asked al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a cleaner man and a jeweler if they were liable. He (the Imam) said, ‘People do not behave well unless they are held liable.’ Yunus would act accordingly and hold liable.’”
